story_spine: A portable native logging core turns an application event into safe, correlated, durable evidence while platform adapters remain replaceable.

selected_context.content: The project should be positioned as a C/C++-based portable logging runtime whose platform adapters can expand beyond the currently implemented mobile stacks, including a future HarmonyOS adapter.

selected_context.source: Core API and asynchronous write-path inspection
selected_context.content: The native core applies level filtering, configurable sanitization, trace context, hooks, serialization, optional encryption, queued I/O, flush semantics, and explicit queue overflow behavior.
Structured binary logs use an mmap-backed append path with bounded writes, file growth, atomic rotation, recovery, retention, and offline parsing support.

panels.purpose: Show replaceable application and platform adapters converging on one portable native contract.

claims.text: Platform adapters are integration surfaces, not the product boundary.

panels.purpose: Expose the safety and correlation work performed before persistence.

claims.text: An event is filtered, sanitized, enriched, and serialized before it reaches storage.

panels.purpose: Show durable local evidence and the recovery path after the write pipeline.

claims.text: The result is bounded local evidence that can rotate, recover, and be parsed offline.

caption_suggestion: The runtime keeps platform integration replaceable while a shared native pipeline turns events into sanitized, trace-correlated, encrypted, and recoverable local evidence.
open_assumptions: HarmonyOS is presented as an extension path, not as an already shipped adapter.
mmap-backed append is described without claiming literal zero-copy behavior or unmeasured throughput.
